title: Hilt, CA on I-5: Exit 796, Northernmost California Exit
meta: Hilt has the northernmost I-5 exit in California, exit 796 at Hilt Road, just south of the 42nd parallel and the Oregon line.
intro: Hilt sits at exit 796 on I-5 and has the northernmost exit in California. It began as a company town, first for the Northern California Lumber Company and then for the Fruit Growers Supply Company, an affiliate of Sunkist. The 42nd parallel, which marks the California and Oregon border, is at mile 797.

faq.q: What exit is Hilt on I-5?
faq.a: Hilt is at exit 796, Hilt Road. It is the northernmost I-5 exit in California.

faq.q: What is the last exit on I-5 in California?
faq.a: The northernmost I-5 exit in California is exit 796 at Hilt. Exit 793, Bailey Hill Road, is the one before it.

faq.q: Where is the California and Oregon border on I-5?
faq.a: The border follows the 42nd parallel, which crosses I-5 at mile 797, just past the Hilt exit. The line was set in an 1819 treaty between the United States and Spain.

faq.q: Is there a rest area near Hilt on I-5?
faq.a: The nearest rest area south of Hilt in the data is Randolph E. Collier Rest Area at mile 785.8, 10.4 miles back. The data lists no rest area north of Hilt, and no gas, food or lodging mapped at the Hilt exits.
